entities.name: Basilica of Saint Severinus of Bordeaux
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Basilica of Saint-Seurin (Saint-Seurin de Bordeaux / Basilica of Saint Severinus of Bordeaux) in Bordeaux, France — one of the oldest Christian sites in France, with continuous sacred use from the 4th century CE through the present — is a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela (1998), a major pre-Romanesque and Romanesque church complex whose crypt contains one of the most important early Christian archaeological ensembles in France.

The site's archaeological significance is extraordinary: excavations under the basilica revealed a 4th-century Christian cemetery and sarcophagi (the 'Paléochrétien' cemetery) containing the remains of early Christian bishops of Bordeaux, some of exceptional quality with carved reliefs depicting early Christian iconography. The sarcophagi are among the most important early Christian funerary monuments in France and provide direct archaeological evidence of 4th-century Christian community life in Gaul.

Saint-Seurin stands on the Via Turonensis — one of the four main Camino de Santiago routes through France — and pilgrims have prayed here for over a millennium on their way to Santiago de Compostela. The church's legendary connection to Roland (Charlemagne's paladin killed at Roncevaux, 778 CE) — pilgrims reportedly left weapons at the church as votive offerings in Roland's memory — gives it a place in the Chansons de Geste literary tradition. The current Romanesque structure (11th-13th century) preserves the ancient crypt with its 4th-century Christian treasures.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Basilica of Saint-Seurin — with France's most important early Christian archaeological ensemble (4th-century sarcophagi), 1,000 years of Camino de Santiago pilgrimage tradition, a Roland legend connection, and UNESCO World Heritage status — is one of France's most historically layered sacred sites.
